dc-1.summary: The revelation opens with a voice calling all people, near and far, to listen. It says disciples chosen in the last days will carry a warning to everyone. It calls itself the Lord’s preface to the book of his commandments. It charges that people have strayed from God’s ordinances and broken his everlasting covenant. It says the Lord, knowing the coming calamity, called Joseph Smith so that “the weak and the simple” could proclaim the gospel. It says the commandments came to servants in their weakness, so their errors could be corrected and their humility rewarded. It calls the church “the only true and living church” and promises forgiveness to those who repent. It ends by telling readers to search these commandments, which it says will all be fulfilled.
dc-1.setting: Joseph Smith received this revelation on 1 November 1831 at Hiram, Ohio, during a conference of elders. The elders had met to plan a published book of his revelations, the Book of Commandments. Minutes say the revelation came during a break between the conference sessions. William McLellin later recalled that the conference rejected a preface drafted by Oliver Cowdery, Sidney Rigdon, and McLellin himself. According to McLellin, Joseph then dictated this preface a few sentences at a time while Rigdon wrote.

verse.text: Behold, I am God and have spoken it; these commandments are of me, and were given unto my servants in their weakness, after the manner of their language, that they might come to understanding.

dc-2.summary: The messenger speaks for the Lord in three short verses. First, the Lord will reveal the priesthood by the hand of Elijah the prophet. This will happen before the great and dreadful day of the Lord. Elijah will plant in the children’s hearts the promises made to the fathers. Then the hearts of the children will turn to their fathers. If this did not happen, the whole earth would be utterly wasted at the Lord’s coming.
dc-2.setting: Section 2 is not a separate revelation text but an excerpt from Joseph Smith’s history. It records words Joseph reported hearing from a heavenly messenger on the night of 21 September 1823, when he was 17. The visit took place in the Smith family’s log home near Palmyra, New York. The official heading identifies the messenger as Moroni, the last keeper of the records that became the Book of Mormon. The messenger quoted Malachi 4:5–6 in a form that differs from the King James Bible. Joseph’s history was written from 1838 on, and these verses joined the Doctrine and Covenants in 1876.

verse.text: And he shall plant in the hearts of the children the promises made to the fathers, and the hearts of the children shall turn to their fathers.

dc-3.summary: The revelation begins by declaring that God’s works and purposes cannot be frustrated. It is the work of men that fails, especially those who boast in their own strength. It then turns to Joseph and recalls how strict his commandments were. It says he gave in to the persuasions of men and feared man more than God. If Joseph repents, he is still chosen; if not, he will lose his gift. He lost his privileges for handing sacred things to a wicked man. Still, the revelation says, the work will go forth. It says the plates were preserved so the Lamanites might know the promises made to their fathers and believe in Christ.
dc-3.setting: From April to June 1828, Joseph Smith dictated the first Book of Mormon manuscript at Harmony, Pennsylvania, with Martin Harris as scribe. Harris pressed to take the 116 pages home to Palmyra, New York, and Joseph finally agreed. Soon after, Emma Smith gave birth to a son who did not survive, and Joseph cared for her for weeks. In early July he went to Palmyra and learned the pages were lost. Joseph’s history says he received this revelation through the Urim and Thummim after returning to Harmony. It is the earliest of his revelations with a surviving text.

verse.text: Remember, remember that it is not the work of God that is frustrated, but the work of men;

dc-4.summary: The revelation announces that a marvelous work is about to come forth. It tells those who enter God’s service to serve with heart, might, mind, and strength. Then it says that desire to serve is itself a call to the work. It compares the moment to a field ready for harvest. The worker who reaps with energy also gains salvation. It lists faith, hope, charity, and love as the qualities that fit a person for the work. It ends with a list of ten virtues and the promise to ask and receive.
dc-4.setting: Joseph Smith Sr. visited his son at Harmony, Pennsylvania, in early 1829. Joseph had apparently not translated the plates since the lost manuscript of June 1828. He dictated this revelation for his father shortly before translation began again. A scribe later corrected the date in Revelation Book 1 from 1828 to 1829.

verse.text: Therefore, if ye have desires to serve God ye are called to the work;

dc-5.summary: The revelation answers Martin Harris’s wish for a witness that Joseph had the plates. It says Joseph covenanted to show the plates only to those the Lord names. His first gift is to translate, and he should claim no other until that is finished. If people will not believe God’s words, they would not believe even if Joseph showed them everything. It promises three witnesses who will be shown the plates by God’s power. Joseph is told to repent and to yield to the persuasions of men no more. Harris can be a witness if he humbles himself in mighty prayer and faith; then he may only say he has seen them. If Harris does not humble himself, Joseph is to translate a few more pages and then stop until commanded again.
dc-5.setting: Martin Harris traveled to Harmony, Pennsylvania, in March 1829. There is no record that he and Joseph Smith had met since the manuscript was lost in 1828. Around Palmyra, opposition to the plates was growing, and Harris’s wife Lucy led much of it. She filed a complaint before a magistrate in Lyons, New York, alleging fraud. Harris came wanting a further witness that Joseph truly had the plates, and this revelation answered his request.

verse.text: Behold, I say unto him, he exalts himself and does not humble himself sufficiently before me; but if he will bow down before me, and humble himself in mighty prayer and faith, in the sincerity of his heart, then will I grant unto him a view of the things which he desires to see.

dc-6.summary: The revelation announces a marvelous work and calls anyone who desires to reap in a ripe field. It tells Oliver to seek wisdom, not riches, and to say nothing but repentance. It tells him to stand by Joseph, to admonish him, and to accept admonition from him. It reminds him that each time he inquired, the Spirit instructed him. It points him to a night when he prayed and received peace in his mind. It offers him a gift to translate, like Joseph, and gives both of them the keys of this gift. Speaking as Jesus Christ, the voice tells them to fear not and do good. It ends by asking them to look to him in every thought and behold his wounds.
dc-6.setting: Oliver Cowdery had boarded with Joseph Smith’s parents near Palmyra, New York. Joseph’s history says Oliver prayed there about the plates and received a confirmation. He arrived in Harmony, Pennsylvania, on 5 April 1829 and began writing as Joseph translated two days later. Some time after, Joseph dictated this revelation, which the heading says came through the Urim and Thummim. It seems to have answered questions Oliver had not voiced to Joseph.

verse.text: Did I not speak peace to your mind concerning the matter? What greater witness can you have than from God?

dc-7.summary: The text is written in John’s own voice. The Lord asks John what he desires, and John asks for power over death to bring souls to Christ. The Lord promises that John will tarry until the Lord comes in glory. The Lord then explains to Peter why John will remain. Peter desired to come quickly to the Lord’s kingdom, and that was a good desire. John desired a greater work among men, so the Lord will make him “as flaming fire and a ministering angel” for the heirs of salvation. Peter will minister for John and James, and the three will hold the keys of this ministry. Both men receive what they desired.
dc-7.setting: In April 1829, Joseph Smith and Oliver Cowdery were translating the Book of Mormon at Harmony, Pennsylvania. They disagreed over whether the apostle John had died or remained on earth. John 21 raises the question but does not settle it. Joseph’s history says they agreed to ask through the Urim and Thummim. Joseph’s history calls it a translation of a parchment John wrote and hid. No account says Joseph had the parchment itself.

verse.text: And the Lord said unto me: Verily, verily, I say unto thee, because thou desirest this thou shalt tarry until I come in my glory, and shalt prophesy before nations, kindreds, tongues and people.

dc-8.summary: The revelation promises Oliver Cowdery knowledge of whatever he asks in faith with an honest heart. It applies this to the engravings of ancient records. It says the Lord will speak to his mind and heart by the Holy Ghost. It calls this the spirit of revelation, the spirit by which Moses led Israel through the Red Sea. It names a second gift, the gift of Aaron, which only God’s power can make work. It warns that without faith he can do nothing and should not ask for what he ought not. It invites him to ask to know mysteries and to translate sacred records.
dc-8.setting: Oliver Cowdery began writing for Joseph Smith at Harmony, Pennsylvania, in April 1829. An earlier revelation, now section 6, had offered him a gift to translate. Oliver wanted that power, and this revelation answered his request. In the earliest copy, his second gift is called working with the “sprout,” or rod. Many people then used such rods to search for water or minerals. Later editions call it the gift of Aaron.

verse.text: Yea, behold, I will tell you in your mind and in your heart, by the Holy Ghost, which shall come upon you and which shall dwell in your heart.

dc-9.summary: The revelation tells Oliver Cowdery to keep writing for Joseph Smith until this record is finished. It promises other records he will later help translate. It says the privilege was taken away because he did not continue as he began. He had supposed it would be given when he only asked. He must study it out in his mind and then ask if it is right. If it is right, his bosom will burn; if not, he will have a stupor of thought. It says he feared, and the time for him to translate has passed. It ends by telling him to stand fast in the work he was called to do.
dc-9.setting: Earlier in April 1829, revelations had promised Oliver Cowdery a gift to translate. He tried at Harmony, Pennsylvania, and did not succeed. This revelation, likely given in the second half of April, explained why. It told him to keep writing for Joseph Smith for now. It also promised he would help translate other records later.

verse.text: But, behold, I say unto you, that you must study it out in your mind; then you must ask me if it be right, and if it is right I will cause that your bosom shall burn within you; therefore, you shall feel that it is right.

dc-10.summary: The revelation reminds Joseph that he lost the writings and his gift by giving them to a wicked man. His gift is now restored, and he is told to pray always and not run faster than his strength allows. It says wicked men have altered the stolen words. Their plan is to wait for a retranslation, then claim the two versions disagree. So Joseph must not translate those words again. Instead he is to translate the fuller account on the plates of Nephi, which covers the same period. The ancient prophets prayed that this gospel would reach the Lamanites and all people in the land. Speaking as Jesus Christ, the voice defines his church as whoever repents and comes to him.
dc-10.setting: In 1828 Martin Harris lost the first 116 pages of the Book of Mormon translation, which Joseph Smith called the Book of Lehi. By spring 1829 Joseph was translating again at Harmony, Pennsylvania, with Oliver Cowdery as scribe. Nearing the end, they weighed whether to retranslate the lost portion. This revelation told Joseph not to. The date is uncertain: the official heading says most likely April 1829, with parts possibly from summer 1828. The Joseph Smith Papers editors suggest part may have come in 1828 but was written down in 1829.

verse.text: I will not suffer that they shall destroy my work; yea, I will show unto them that my wisdom is greater than the cunning of the devil.

dc-11.summary: The revelation opens with the same call to the harvest given to Oliver Cowdery in section 6. It tells Hyrum to seek wisdom, not riches, and to say nothing but repentance. It says he will have a gift if he asks in faith with an honest heart. It tells him to trust the Spirit that leads to do good, do justly, walk humbly, and judge righteously. That Spirit will enlighten his mind and fill his soul with joy. He is not to preach until he is called. First he must obtain the word, studying what has gone forth and what is now being translated. Speaking as Jesus Christ, the voice promises power to become sons of God to all who receive him.
dc-11.setting: Hyrum Smith, Joseph Smith’s older brother, came to Harmony, Pennsylvania, in May 1829 to learn about the work. Joseph inquired through the Urim and Thummim and received this revelation for him. Joseph’s history places it after the restoration of the Aaronic Priesthood, which he dated to 15 May 1829. Joseph Smith Papers notes suggest it came after Samuel Smith’s baptism, perhaps on 25 May. The pages of Revelation Book 1 that held it are missing.

verse.text: Seek not to declare my word, but first seek to obtain my word, and then shall your tongue be loosed; then, if you desire, you shall have my Spirit and my word, yea, the power of God unto the convincing of men.

dc-12.summary: The revelation opens by announcing that a great and marvelous work is about to come forth. The voice speaks as God and calls its word sharper than a two-edged sword. It says the field is ready for harvest, and whoever reaps with might is called of God. It promises that those who ask will receive. Because Knight has asked, it tells him to keep the commandments and help establish the cause of Zion. It then says no one can assist unless humble, loving, faithful, hopeful, charitable, and temperate. It closes with the speaker naming himself the light and life of the world.
dc-12.setting: Joseph Knight Sr. was a farmer and miller from Colesville, New York. He had helped Joseph Smith with food, money, and paper since 1827. In May 1829 Joseph and Oliver Cowdery ran short of supplies at Harmony, Pennsylvania. Knight soon came to Harmony with paper and enough food to finish the translation. Joseph’s history says Knight was anxious to know his duty, so Joseph asked the Lord for him. The exact day of Knight’s arrival is not recorded.

verse.text: And no one can assist in this work except he shall be humble and full of love, having faith, hope, and charity, being temperate in all things, whatsoever shall be entrusted to his care.

dc-13.summary: These are the words of an ordination, not a full revelation. The speaker calls Joseph and Oliver his “fellow servants.” He confers the Priesthood of Aaron in the name of Messiah. He says this priesthood holds the keys of the ministering of angels. It also holds the keys of the gospel of repentance and of baptism by immersion for remission of sins. He says it will not be taken from the earth until the sons of Levi again offer an offering in righteousness.
dc-13.setting: Joseph Smith and Oliver Cowdery were translating the Book of Mormon at Harmony, Pennsylvania. Joseph’s later history says the text raised a question about baptism for the remission of sins. On 15 May 1829 the two men went into the woods near the Susquehanna River to pray about it. They reported that an angel who called himself John, the Baptist of the New Testament, ordained them. This section is the ordination wording as recorded in Joseph’s history, written years later.

verse.text: Upon you my fellow servants, in the name of Messiah I confer the Priesthood of Aaron, which holds the keys of the ministering of angels, and of the gospel of repentance, and of baptism by immersion for the remission of sins; and this shall never be taken again from the earth, until the sons of Levi do offer again an offering unto the Lord in righteousness.

dc-14.summary: The revelation opens with the same words given to Joseph Knight and others: a marvelous work is about to come forth. It says the field is ready to harvest and whoever reaps is called. It tells David to seek to establish Zion and keep the commandments in all things. If he endures to the end, he will have eternal life, the greatest gift of God. If he asks the Father in faith, he will receive the Holy Ghost. The Spirit will help him witness what he hears and sees and declare repentance. The speaker names himself Jesus Christ and says the gospel must go from the Gentiles to Israel. It ends by telling David he is called to assist and will be blessed if faithful.
dc-14.setting: In late May or early June 1829, David Whitmer drove his wagon to Harmony, Pennsylvania. He moved Joseph Smith and Oliver Cowdery to his father Peter Whitmer Sr.’s farm in Fayette, New York. There Joseph worked to finish translating the Book of Mormon. David and his brothers John and Peter Jr. became eager helpers and wanted to know their duties. Joseph’s history says he asked the Lord through the Urim and Thummim, and this revelation for David came first. Its wording suggests David had already been baptized that month.

verse.text: And, if you keep my commandments and endure to the end you shall have eternal life, which gift is the greatest of all the gifts of God.

routes.title: Joseph and Oliver move from Harmony to Fayette

dc-15.summary: The revelation addresses John by name and speaks as Jesus Christ, his Lord and Redeemer. It says the Lord speaks with sharpness and power. It says it will tell John something only he and the Lord know. John has many times wanted to know what would be of most worth to him. The revelation blesses him for that desire and for speaking the Lord’s words. It then answers: the thing of most worth is to declare repentance. By doing so he may bring souls to Christ and rest with them in the Father’s kingdom.
dc-15.setting: John Whitmer was 26 and living at his father’s farm in Fayette, New York. Joseph Smith was there in June 1829 finishing the Book of Mormon translation. John sometimes wrote as scribe when Oliver Cowdery was away. He was probably baptized that month, and he asked Joseph to inquire about his duty. This revelation answered him, and an identical one went to his brother Peter Jr.

verse.text: And now, behold, I say unto you, that the thing which will be of the most worth unto you will be to declare repentance unto this people, that you may bring souls unto me, that you may rest with them in the kingdom of my Father. Amen.

routes.title: Joseph and Oliver move from Harmony to Fayette

dc-16.summary: The revelation addresses Peter by name and speaks as Jesus Christ, his Lord and Redeemer. It says the Lord speaks with sharpness and power, and his arm is over all the earth. It promises to tell Peter something only he and the Lord know. Peter has often wanted to know what would be of most worth to him. The revelation blesses him for that desire and for speaking the Lord’s words. It answers that declaring repentance is of most worth. By that work he may bring souls to Christ and rest with them in the Father’s kingdom.
dc-16.setting: Peter Whitmer Jr. was a 19-year-old tailor living at his father’s farm in Fayette, New York. He was baptized in Seneca Lake in June 1829. Like his brothers David and John, he wanted to know his duty in the work. Joseph Smith dictated this revelation for him in early June. It matches word for word the one given to John, which seems to have come first.

verse.text: For many times you have desired of me to know that which would be of the most worth unto you.

routes.title: Joseph and Oliver move from Harmony to Fayette

dc-17.summary: The revelation tells the three men to rely on the Lord’s word with full purpose of heart. If they do, they will see the plates, breastplate, sword of Laban, Urim and Thummim, and Lehi’s directors. It says they will see these things by faith, like the prophets of old. Afterward they must testify of them by the power of God. Their testimony will help keep Joseph Smith from being destroyed. They will testify that they have seen as Joseph has seen. The voice declares that the translated book is true. If they obey, the gates of hell will not prevail against them.
dc-17.setting: Joseph Smith finished translating the Book of Mormon at Fayette, New York, in June 1829. The translation said three witnesses would see the plates and testify of them. Oliver Cowdery, David Whitmer, and Martin Harris each wanted to be one of them. Joseph inquired through the Urim and Thummim, and this revelation was the answer. Joseph later said that not many days after, the four men went into the woods to pray for the promised view. The earliest surviving copy dates from no earlier than late 1834 and may have been edited.

verse.text: And after that you have obtained faith, and have seen them with your eyes, you shall testify of them, by the power of God;

routes.title: Joseph and Oliver move from Harmony to Fayette

dc-18.summary: The revelation tells Oliver Cowdery that what he has written is true and commands him to rely on it. It says the written record holds the foundation of the Church and gospel. It confirms Oliver’s baptism by Joseph Smith and says Joseph is called for the Lord’s purpose. It calls Oliver and David Whitmer to cry repentance, with the same calling as Paul. It explains that the worth of souls is great because the Redeemer suffered for all. It describes the joy of bringing even one soul to Christ. It then speaks of twelve disciples who will take Christ’s name, preach, and baptize. Oliver and David are told to search out the Twelve by their desires and works.
dc-18.setting: Joseph Smith dictated this revelation at Fayette, New York, in the first part of June 1829. It came after David Whitmer’s baptism and before a 14 June letter from Oliver Cowdery. It answers something Oliver wanted to know and speaks to him and David Whitmer. Joseph later said it made known the calling of twelve apostles and how to build up the Church. Later that month Oliver drafted “Articles of the Church of Christ,” drawn largely from the Book of Mormon.

verse.text: Remember the worth of souls is great in the sight of God;

routes.title: Joseph and Oliver move from Harmony to Fayette

dc-19.summary: The revelation opens with the speaker naming himself Alpha and Omega, Christ the Lord. It says every person must repent or suffer. It explains that “endless” and “eternal” punishment mean God’s punishment, because Endless is his name. It commands Martin Harris to repent, describing Christ’s own suffering that made him bleed at every pore. It tells Harris to preach only repentance for now. It commands him not to covet his property but to pay for printing the Book of Mormon. It tells him to pray aloud as well as in secret and to declare glad tidings. It ends by telling him to pay the printer, release himself from bondage, and come to Christ.
dc-19.setting: Martin Harris was a prosperous farmer near Palmyra, New York. He had agreed to pay the Palmyra printer Egbert Grandin to print the Book of Mormon. Grandin’s price for five thousand copies was $3,000, nearly all of Harris’s property. This revelation, given through Joseph Smith at Manchester, urged Harris to pay. On 25 August 1829 Harris mortgaged his farm to Grandin. Early printings dated the revelation March 1830, but historians now favor summer 1829.

verse.text: For behold, I, God, have suffered these things for all, that they might not suffer if they would repent;

dc-20.summary: The document opens by dating the Church’s organization to 6 April 1830. It names Joseph Smith as first elder and Oliver Cowdery as second elder. It recounts Joseph’s forgiveness, his return to worldly vanities, an angel’s visit, and the translation of the Book of Mormon. It then states core beliefs about God, the Fall, Christ’s atonement, justification, and sanctification. It sets the requirements for baptism. It lists the duties of apostles and elders, priests, teachers, and deacons. It gives the exact words for baptism and for blessing the bread and wine. It closes with rules for conferences, records, licenses, and members who move.
dc-20.setting: This document was known in Joseph Smith’s day as the Articles and Covenants. Joseph may have begun it in summer 1829, near the time Oliver Cowdery drafted his own articles. The earliest copies already describe the Church as organized on 6 April 1830, so parts were written or revised afterward. It was likely composed at or near Fayette, New York. At the first Church conference on 9 June 1830, Joseph read it and members approved it unanimously.

verse.text: And again, by way of commandment to the church concerning the manner of baptism—All those who humble themselves before God, and desire to be baptized, and come forth with broken hearts and contrite spirits, and witness before the church that they have truly repented of all their sins, and are willing to take upon them the name of Jesus Christ, having a determination to serve him to the end, and truly manifest by their works that they have received of the Spirit of Christ unto the remission of their sins, shall be received by baptism into his church.

dc-21.summary: The revelation commands that a record be kept. In it Joseph Smith is to be called a seer, translator, prophet, apostle, and elder. It dates the Church’s organization to 6 April 1830. It tells the Church to heed Joseph’s words as if from the Lord’s own mouth, in patience and faith. If they do, the gates of hell will not prevail against them. It says the Lord has seen Joseph’s weeping for Zion and has forgiven him. It directs Oliver Cowdery to ordain Joseph. It calls Oliver an elder under Joseph’s hand and the Church’s first preacher.
dc-21.setting: On 6 April 1830 Joseph Smith and others met at Peter Whitmer Sr.’s home in Fayette, New York, to organize the Church. The group voted unanimously to accept Joseph and Oliver Cowdery as their teachers. Joseph ordained Oliver an elder, and Oliver ordained Joseph. They took bread and wine and laid hands on those present to confirm them. While the group was still together, Joseph dictated this revelation. Some early sources placed the event in Manchester, but the earliest manuscript and eyewitnesses support Fayette.

verse.text: For his word ye shall receive, as if from mine own mouth, in all patience and faith.

dc-22.summary: The revelation says all old covenants have been done away in this thing. It calls baptism into the Church a new and everlasting covenant that was from the beginning. It says a person baptized a hundred times gains nothing by it. No one can enter the strait gate by the law of Moses or by dead works. It says these dead works are why the Lord has built up this last covenant and church. It ends by telling them to enter at the gate as commanded and not to counsel God.
dc-22.setting: Ten days after the Church was organized, some believers wanted to join without being baptized again. Orson Pratt later described them as moral Baptists who accepted the Book of Mormon. Joseph Smith asked the Lord and dictated this revelation on 16 April 1830. The official heading places it at Manchester, New York, while the Joseph Smith Papers place it in Fayette Township. Early copyists often attached it to the Articles and Covenants as part of the baptism rules.

verse.text: Wherefore, although a man should be baptized an hundred times it availeth him nothing, for you cannot enter in at the strait gate by the law of Moses, neither by your dead works.

dc-23.summary: These are five brief revelations gathered into one section. Oliver Cowdery is told he is under no condemnation but must beware of pride. He is to make his calling known to the Church and the world. Hyrum Smith is also under no condemnation and is called to exhort and strengthen the Church. His duty is to the Church forever, because of his family. Samuel H. Smith is called to exhort and strengthen the Church but not yet to preach to the world. Joseph Smith Sr. is called to exhort and strengthen the Church from then on. Joseph Knight Sr. is told to take up his cross and pray aloud in every setting. He is also told it is his duty to unite with the true church.
dc-23.setting: Soon after the Church was organized on 6 April 1830, five men asked Joseph Smith to learn their duties. They were Oliver Cowdery, Hyrum Smith, Samuel H. Smith, Joseph Smith Sr., and Joseph Knight Sr. Joseph dictated five short revelations, apparently one after another. The official heading places them at Manchester, New York. The Joseph Smith Papers place the related meetings in Fayette Township and suggest they came before an 11 April meeting.

verse.text: Behold, I manifest unto you, Joseph Knight, by these words, that you must take up your cross, in the which you must pray vocally before the world as well as in secret, and in your family, and among your friends, and in all places.

dc-24.summary: The revelation reminds Joseph that he was called to write the Book of Mormon and has been delivered from his enemies. It says he is not excused for his sins, but he should go and sin no more. After he sows and secures his fields, he is to visit the branches at Colesville, Fayette, and Manchester. If they receive him they will be blessed; if not, they will be cursed. His work is to pray, write what the Comforter gives, and expound the scriptures. Verse 9 says he will not have strength in temporal labors, because that is not his calling. Oliver is to keep declaring the gospel to the church and the world. Both men are to work miracles only when asked, take no purse or scrip, and let the church supply their needs.
dc-24.setting: This revelation came to Joseph Smith and Oliver Cowdery at Harmony, Pennsylvania, in July 1830. The church was less than four months old. In late June and early July, Joseph was arrested twice near Colesville, New York, and released both times. When he and Oliver went back to confirm new converts, a mob drove them away. The revelation was one of three given in this tense period, and its exact day is not recorded.

verse.text: And in temporal labors thou shalt not have strength, for this is not thy calling. Attend to thy calling and thou shalt have wherewith to magnify thine office, and to expound all scriptures, and continue in laying on of the hands and confirming the churches.

dc-25.summary: The revelation speaks to Emma Smith as a daughter in the Lord’s kingdom. It promises to preserve her life and give her an inheritance in Zion if she is faithful. It forgives her sins and calls her “an elect lady”. It tells her not to murmur over things she has not been shown. Her calling is to comfort Joseph, serve as his scribe, and be ordained to expound scripture and exhort the church. She is to lay aside the things of this world and make a selection of sacred hymns. The text warns against pride and promises a crown of righteousness if she keeps the commandments. It closes by saying this is the Lord’s voice to all.
dc-25.setting: Joseph Smith dictated this revelation for his wife, Emma Hale Smith, at Harmony, Pennsylvania, in July 1830. Emma had been baptized at Colesville, New York, on 28 June, but opposition delayed her confirmation. The earliest manuscript gives only the year, and the July date first appears in the 1833 Book of Commandments. It was the first known revelation of Joseph’s addressed to a woman. In 1835 Emma and William W. Phelps compiled the church’s first hymnal.

verse.text: For my soul delighteth in the song of the heart; yea, the song of the righteous is a prayer unto me, and it shall be answered with a blessing upon their heads.

dc-26.summary: The revelation tells the three men how to spend their time until the next conference. They are to study the scriptures and preach. They are to confirm the church at Colesville. They are also to do the work needed on the land. After they go west to hold the conference, further direction will be given. Verse 2 then states a general rule: all things in the church are to be done by common consent, with much prayer and faith.
dc-26.setting: This short revelation came at Harmony, Pennsylvania, in July 1830. It was addressed to Joseph Smith, Oliver Cowdery, and John Whitmer. It came shortly after section 24, which told Joseph to tend his fields and then visit the branches. Joseph’s church work had left him little time for his farm. The Joseph Smith Papers editors supply the month, and no exact day is recorded.

verse.text: And all things shall be done by common consent in the church, by much prayer and faith, for all things you shall receive by faith. Amen.

dc-27.summary: The revelation speaks as Jesus Christ. It says that what the Saints eat or drink in the sacrament does not matter if they remember his body and blood. It forbids buying wine or strong drink from enemies and allows only wine made new among themselves. It promises that Christ will drink of the fruit of the vine with his servants on the earth. It names those who will join him: Moroni, Elias, John the Baptist, Elijah, the patriarchs, Michael or Adam, and Peter, James, and John. It says John ordained Joseph Smith and Oliver Cowdery to the first priesthood. It says Peter, James, and John ordained them apostles and gave them keys. It ends by telling them to put on “my whole armor” and stand.
dc-27.setting: In August 1830, Newel and Sally Knight visited Joseph and Emma Smith at Harmony, Pennsylvania. Emma and Sally had not yet been confirmed, and the group planned to confirm them and take the sacrament. Joseph reported that a heavenly messenger met him as he went to buy wine. He wrote the first paragraph then; his later history says the rest was written in September. The longer text was first printed in the 1835 Doctrine and Covenants.

verse.text: For, behold, I say unto you, that it mattereth not what ye shall eat or what ye shall drink when ye partake of the sacrament, if it so be that ye do it with an eye single to my glory—remembering unto the Father my body which was laid down for you, and my blood which was shed for the remission of your sins.

dc-28.summary: The revelation tells Oliver Cowdery the church will hear him when he teaches by the Comforter. It then says only Joseph Smith is appointed to receive commandments and revelations for the church, “even as Moses”. Oliver is to be like Aaron, declaring what Joseph receives. He may speak by the Spirit, but he must not write by way of commandment or command Joseph. Oliver is sent to preach to the Lamanites and establish the church among them. The city of Zion’s location is not yet revealed, but it will be “on the borders by the Lamanites”. Oliver is to tell Hiram Page privately that his stone writings come from Satan. All things are to be done in order and by common consent.
dc-28.setting: This revelation came at Fayette, New York, in September 1830, shortly before the conference of 26 September. Joseph and Emma Smith had just moved there from Harmony, Pennsylvania. Hiram Page claimed to receive revelations through a stone about Zion and church order. Many members, including Oliver Cowdery and the Whitmer family, accepted them. Earlier that summer Oliver had written commanding Joseph to erase words from the church’s Articles and Covenants. Joseph sought guidance and dictated this revelation for Oliver.

verse.text: But, behold, verily, verily, I say unto thee, no one shall be appointed to receive commandments and revelations in this church excepting my servant Joseph Smith, Jun., for he receiveth them even as Moses.

dc-29.summary: The revelation speaks as Jesus Christ, who will gather his people “as a hen gathereth her chickens”. It forgives the elders and calls them to gather the elect to one place on this land. It describes Christ’s coming in glory, the Twelve judging Israel, and the rising of the righteous dead. Signs, plagues, and the fall of the great and abominable church come first. After the thousand years, a new heaven and earth replace the old. The text then says all of God’s commandments are spiritual, not temporal. It explains the devil’s rebellion, Adam’s fall, and the time of probation given for repentance. It says little children are redeemed through Christ and cannot sin until they become accountable.
dc-29.setting: This revelation came at Fayette, New York, in September 1830, a few days before the 26 September conference. Six elders and three other members were present. Revelation Book 1 says they differed over Adam’s transgression and asked the Lord about it. Many members were also eager about the Book of Mormon’s promise of a gathering in America. Hiram Page’s competing revelations about Zion were circulating at the same time.

verse.text: And it must needs be that the devil should tempt the children of men, or they could not be agents unto themselves; for if they never should have bitter they could not know the sweet—

dc-30.summary: The revelation first rebukes David Whitmer for fearing man and thinking on earthly things. It says he has been persuaded by people the Lord did not command. He is to stay at his father’s house, ponder, and serve in the church nearby. Peter Whitmer Jr. is told to go with Oliver Cowdery on the mission to the Lamanites. He is to heed Oliver and pray for him in his afflictions. Only Joseph Smith is named as Oliver’s counselor in church matters. John Whitmer is told to begin preaching at once. His labor is to be at Philip Burroughs’ home and the region around it.
dc-30.setting: These three revelations came at Fayette, New York, in late September 1830. They followed the church’s second conference, which began on 26 September, before the elders dispersed. Each was addressed to one Whitmer brother: David, Peter Jr., and John. The conference had named David church record keeper, though his revelation does not mention it. The 1835 Doctrine and Covenants first combined the three texts into one section.

verse.text: But your mind has been on the things of the earth more than on the things of me, your Maker, and the ministry whereunto you have been called; and you have not given heed unto my Spirit, and to those who were set over you, but have been persuaded by those whom I have not commanded.

dc-31.summary: The revelation blesses Thomas Marsh for his faith in the work. It recognizes his afflictions because of his family and promises they will one day believe and join him. It says the hour of his mission has come and his tongue will be loosed. He is to preach what was revealed to Joseph Smith and reap in a field “white already to be burned.” It says his sins are forgiven and his family shall live. He is to leave them only a little while, and the Lord will prepare a place for them. He will establish a church and be a physician to the church, but not to the world. He is told to be patient, govern his house in meekness, pray always, and be faithful to the end.
dc-31.setting: Joseph Smith dictated this revelation for Thomas B. Marsh in September 1830. Joseph’s history ties it to the church conference at Fayette, New York, that began on 26 September. Marsh had first learned of the Book of Mormon in 1829, while it was being printed in Palmyra. He moved his family from Massachusetts to Palmyra in September 1830. Shortly before the conference, David Whitmer baptized him and Oliver Cowdery ordained him an elder.

verse.text: Behold, verily I say unto you, go from them only for a little time, and declare my word, and I will prepare a place for them.

dc-32.summary: The revelation says Parley P. Pratt is to declare the gospel, learn of the Lord, and be meek and lowly of heart. He is to go with Oliver Cowdery and Peter Whitmer Jr. into the wilderness among the Lamanites. Ziba Peterson is to go with them as well. The Lord says he will go with them and be their advocate with the Father. Nothing shall prevail against them. They are to heed what is written and claim no other revelation. They are to pray always that the written word will be opened to their understanding.
dc-32.setting: In September 1830, Oliver Cowdery and Peter Whitmer Jr. were called to preach to the Lamanites, meaning American Indians in the West. Other elders wanted these peoples to hear the Book of Mormon too, so Joseph Smith asked whether more should go. This revelation answered at Manchester, New York, in October 1830, probably before 17 October. It named Parley P. Pratt, baptized only weeks earlier, and Ziba Peterson, an elder licensed in June 1830. The missionaries left in late October and reached the Missouri border early in 1831.

verse.text: And they shall give heed to that which is written, and pretend to no other revelation; and they shall pray always that I may unfold the same to their understanding.

dc-33.summary: The revelation calls Ezra Thayre and Northrop Sweet to hear the Lord’s word, “sharper than a two-edged sword”. It sends them to declare the gospel to a crooked and perverse generation. It says the field is white for harvest and this is the eleventh hour. It describes the vineyard as corrupted, with many led astray by priestcrafts. The Lord says he has called this church out of the wilderness and will gather his elect. The men are told to open their mouths, and they will be filled. Their message is repentance, baptism by water, and the baptism of fire and the Holy Ghost. They are to keep the church articles, use the Book of Mormon and the scriptures, and be ready for the Bridegroom.
dc-33.setting: Joseph Smith dictated this revelation at Fayette, New York, in early October 1830. It was for Ezra Thayre and Northrop Sweet, both baptized within the previous month. It called them to the ministry and told them how to preach. Thayre later recalled a vision that prepared him for it, though he told this decades afterward. Sweet soon left the church and helped form a small group called the Pure Church of Christ.

verse.text: Open your mouths and they shall be filled, and you shall become even as Nephi of old, who journeyed from Jerusalem in the wilderness.

dc-34.summary: The voice in the revelation speaks as Jesus Christ, the light of the world. It recalls that he gave his life so believers might become God’s sons. On that basis it calls Orson his son. Orson is blessed for believing and more blessed for being called to preach. He is told to cry repentance loudly to a “crooked and perverse generation”. The revelation describes signs before Christ’s coming: a darkened sun, a blood-red moon, and falling stars. It tells Orson to prophesy by the Holy Ghost and promises to be with him if he is faithful.
dc-34.setting: Orson Pratt was baptized by his older brother Parley on 19 September 1830, his nineteenth birthday. In October he traveled more than 200 miles to Fayette, New York, where Joseph Smith was staying. He asked Joseph to inquire of the Lord about his duty. Joseph dictated this revelation on 4 November 1830 in Orson’s presence, and John Whitmer wrote it down. Orson was ordained an elder about a month later and began preaching in Colesville.

verse.text: Who so loved the world that he gave his own life, that as many as would believe might become the sons of God. Wherefore you are my son;

dc-35.summary: The voice speaks as Jesus Christ, crucified so believers may become one with him as he is with the Father. It tells Sidney Rigdon that God has seen his works and prepared him for a greater work. It compares him to John, sent to prepare the way without knowing it. He had baptized without the Holy Ghost following; now those he baptizes will receive it by laying on of hands. The revelation promises miracles to believers and says the weak and unlearned will thresh the nations. It says the gospel came through Joseph, blessed in weakness, who holds keys while he abides in Christ. Sidney is to watch over Joseph, write for him, and not forsake him. If Sidney does not write, Joseph will prophesy and Sidney will preach and prove his words from the prophets.
dc-35.setting: Sidney Rigdon led a reformed Baptist congregation in northeastern Ohio. In November 1830 missionaries preached there, and Rigdon and many members joined the Church. In early December Rigdon and Edward Partridge traveled to New York to meet Joseph Smith. Joseph dictated this revelation on 7 December 1830 at or near Fayette. He had been revising the Bible since June 1830, and his earlier scribes had other duties.

verse.text: And a commandment I give unto thee—that thou shalt write for him; and the scriptures shall be given, even as they are in mine own bosom, to the salvation of mine own elect;

dc-36.summary: The voice speaks as the Lord God and tells Edward that his sins are forgiven. Edward is called to preach as with the voice of a trumpet. Sidney Rigdon is to lay hands on him so he receives the Holy Ghost. Edward is to cry, “Hosanna, blessed be the name of the most high God”. Then the revelation widens its call to all men. Anyone who comes to Sidney Rigdon and Joseph Smith embracing this call may be ordained and sent out. It closes with the voice, as Jesus Christ, saying he will suddenly come to his temple.
dc-36.setting: Edward Partridge was a hatter from Painesville, Ohio, and a member of Sidney Rigdon’s congregation. His wife, Lydia, joined the Church after missionaries preached there in November 1830. Edward wanted to meet Joseph Smith first, so he came to New York with Rigdon and then asked for baptism. Joseph dictated this revelation for him on 9 December 1830 near Fayette. Joseph baptized him on 11 December, and Rigdon ordained him an elder on 15 December.

verse.text: And this commandment shall be given unto the elders of my church, that every man which will embrace it with singleness of heart may be ordained and sent forth, even as I have spoken.

dc-37.summary: The revelation tells Joseph and Sidney to stop translating until they go to the Ohio. It gives two reasons: “because of the enemy” and “for your sakes”. First they must preach and strengthen the branches, especially in Colesville. It says the Colesville members pray in much faith. Then it commands the Church to assemble in the Ohio before Oliver Cowdery returns. It ends by telling every man to choose for himself.
dc-37.setting: In late December 1830 Joseph Smith and Sidney Rigdon were working on Joseph’s revision of the Bible. The Joseph Smith Papers place this revelation at Canandaigua, New York, about 30 December, soon after they arrived there. The official heading places it near Fayette in December 1830. Opposition to the Church was growing in New York, especially in Colesville. Oliver Cowdery was then leading the mission to the Lamanites, bound for western Missouri.

verse.text: And again, a commandment I give unto the church, that it is expedient in me that they should assemble together at the Ohio, against the time that my servant Oliver Cowdery shall return unto them.

routes.title: The New York Saints gather to Ohio

dc-38.summary: The voice speaks as Jesus Christ, the Creator, who took the Zion of Enoch to himself. It warns that the wicked are kept in chains of darkness for judgment. It tells the Saints he is in their midst though unseen, and that some are clean but not all. It reveals that enemies in “secret chambers” plot their destruction. It promises a land of inheritance if they seek it with all their hearts. It commands each person to esteem his brother as himself and gives a parable of a father who favors one son. It then explains the move: in Ohio they will receive the law and be “endowed with power from on high”. Men chosen by the Church will care for the poor and property, and all are to warn neighbors meekly.
dc-38.setting: The Church held its third conference at Fayette, New York, on 2 January 1831. Three days earlier a revelation had told members to gather in Ohio. Members at the conference wanted to know more, so Joseph Smith inquired before the congregation. Some were reluctant to move, and John Whitmer recorded that some suspected Joseph of inventing the command for gain. A Waterloo writer reported that property owners resisted at first but agreed after fasting and prayer.

verse.text: Behold, this I have given unto you as a parable, and it is even as I am. I say unto you, be one; and if ye are not one ye are not mine.

routes.title: The New York Saints gather to Ohio

dc-39.summary: The voice speaks as Jesus Christ, who gives power to become his sons to all who receive him. It defines the gospel as repentance, baptism by water, and then the baptism of fire and the Holy Ghost. It tells James that his heart is right at this time. It also says he has rejected the Lord many times because of pride and worldly cares. If he will arise and be baptized, it promises a blessing greater than he has known. It calls him to preach, but in the Ohio, not in the eastern countries. It says the Ohio people pray in faith, and judgment will be stayed only if they repent. James is to baptize and lay on hands for the gift of the Holy Ghost.
dc-39.setting: On 5 January 1831, three days after the Church conference, Joseph Smith dictated this revelation at Fayette, New York. It was for a minister named James, who had covenanted to obey any command given through Joseph. Later printings name him James Covel or Covill. The Joseph Smith Papers favor James Covel, a Methodist elder near Canandaigua, but no source settles his identity.

verse.text: Nevertheless, thou hast seen great sorrow, for thou hast rejected me many times because of pride and the cares of the world.

dc-40.summary: The revelation says James Covel’s heart had been right, for he covenanted to obey the Lord’s word. He received the word with gladness. It says Satan tempted him straightway. The fear of persecution and the cares of the world led him to reject the word. So he broke the covenant. The revelation leaves his outcome with the Lord, to do “as seemeth me good”.
dc-40.setting: James Covel left Fayette within a day of the 5 January revelation, without explaining why. Joseph Smith and Sidney Rigdon were left asking why he had not obeyed. Joseph later recalled that this revelation, dated 6 January 1831, gave the reason. His history says Covel returned to his former principles and people.

verse.text: And he received the word with gladness, but straightway Satan tempted him; and the fear of persecution and the cares of the world caused him to reject the word.

dc-41.summary: The revelation addresses the elders as people the Lord delights to bless. It commands them to assemble and agree on his word. By the prayer of faith they will receive his law to govern the Church. Whoever receives the law and does it is a disciple; whoever claims it but does not is not. It says Joseph should have a house built in which to live and translate. Sidney Rigdon may live as he thinks best while he keeps the commandments. Edward Partridge is to be appointed by the Church’s voice and ordained a bishop. He is to leave his business, for his heart is pure like Nathanael’s, a man without guile.
dc-41.setting: Joseph Smith arrived in Kirtland, Ohio, from New York on 4 February 1831 and dictated this revelation that day. Leman Copley, a recent convert, had offered Joseph and Sidney Rigdon houses and provisions on his farm in Thompson. John Whitmer’s heading links the revelation to that offer, though later histories tie it to excesses among new converts. The revelation also named Edward Partridge bishop, the first known use of that title in the Church.

verse.text: He that receiveth my law and doeth it, the same is my disciple; and he that saith he receiveth it and doeth it not, the same is not my disciple, and shall be cast out from among you;

dc-42.summary: The revelation calls itself a law and first sends every elder except Joseph Smith and Sidney Rigdon to preach two by two. Edward Partridge keeps his office, and no one may preach unless ordained by someone with known authority. Teachers are to teach from the Bible and the Book of Mormon, and only by the Spirit. Then it gives moral laws against killing, stealing, lying, lust, adultery, and speaking evil. It commands the Saints to consecrate property to the bishop for the poor, each becoming a steward of what he receives. Surplus goes to a storehouse for the needy, for lands, and for building the New Jerusalem. It adds rules on plain dress, idleness, care for the sick, and seeking revelation. The later verses set procedures for church discipline and for handing crimes to the law of the land.
dc-42.setting: Joseph Smith had reached Kirtland, Ohio, only days earlier, and many new converts were waiting for direction. Earlier revelations had promised that the law would be given once the Saints gathered in Ohio. On 9 February 1831 twelve elders met, prayed together, and asked practical questions about gathering, governance, and property. Joseph dictated verses 1–72 in their presence. The Joseph Smith Papers date verses 74–93 to 23 February, when Joseph and seven elders asked how to apply the law.

verse.text: And behold, thou wilt remember the poor, and consecrate of thy properties for their support that which thou hast to impart unto them, with a covenant and a deed which cannot be broken.

dc-43.summary: The revelation tells the elders they have received a law through the one appointed to receive revelations. No one else is appointed to that gift while he abides in the Lord. If it is taken from him, his only power is to appoint another in his place. The elders are not to accept anyone else’s teachings as revelations. When assembled, they are to instruct and edify each other and sanctify themselves. They are to uphold Joseph and provide his food and clothing. Then it turns to the coming day of the Lord, when thunders, lightnings, and God’s voice call the nations to repent. It describes the Millennium, Satan bound, and the earth passing away, and ends, “Be sober”.
dc-43.setting: In February 1831 Joseph Smith was newly settled in Kirtland, Ohio. The Ohio converts had gone months without experienced leaders. A woman remembered as Mrs. Hubble, probably Louisa Hubbell, claimed to receive commandments for the Church, and some members believed her. Joseph inquired of the Lord, and this revelation was the reply. The Joseph Smith Papers date it between 9 February and the end of the month.

verse.text: And this ye shall know assuredly—that there is none other appointed unto you to receive commandments and revelations until he be taken, if he abide in me.

dc-44.summary: The revelation says the elders should be called together from every direction, by letter or other means. If they are faithful, the Spirit will be poured out when they assemble. They will then preach repentance in the nearby regions. Many will be converted, giving the Saints power to organize under the laws of man. That organization will protect them from enemies and help them keep God’s laws. Finally the elders must visit the poor and needy and relieve them until all is done by the law.
dc-44.setting: Joseph Smith dictated this revelation in Kirtland, Ohio, in the latter part of February 1831. It is addressed to Joseph Smith and Sidney Rigdon. A letter Joseph wrote to Martin Harris on 22 February seems to allude to it, so it likely came before that date. The Church later set a conference for early June 1831, which Joseph’s history links to this call.

verse.text: And many shall be converted, insomuch that ye shall obtain power to organize yourselves according to the laws of man;

dc-45.summary: The revelation opens with the voice of the Creator calling the Church to listen. It presents Christ as an advocate pleading with the Father for those who believe. It then repeats what Jesus told his disciples about the coming fall of the Jerusalem temple. It describes wars, sickness, earthquakes, and a gospel light that many reject. The disciples are told not to be troubled, and a fig tree parable shows how to read the signs. It describes Christ’s return, the Jews seeing his wounds, and the wise who abide the day. It then tells Joseph to translate the New Testament. Finally, it calls the elders to gather west and build the New Jerusalem, a city of refuge called Zion.
dc-45.setting: Joseph Smith dictated this revelation at Kirtland, Ohio, around 7 March 1831. Two early copies date it 6 March instead. His later history says false newspaper reports were then circulating to discourage interest in the Church. He described the revelation as a source of joy to the Saints. It is addressed to the whole Church.

verse.text: And I said unto them: Be not troubled, for, when all these things shall come to pass, ye may know that the promises which have been made unto you shall be fulfilled.

dc-46.summary: The revelation says elders should lead meetings as the Holy Spirit directs. It forbids casting anyone out of public meetings. Earnest seekers who are not members may stay in sacrament and confirmation meetings. Members who have sinned should not take the sacrament until they make reconciliation. It warns against deception and tells members to “seek ye earnestly the best gifts”. It then lists gifts of the Spirit, from knowing that Jesus Christ is the Son of God to interpreting tongues. The bishop and appointed elders are to discern these gifts. It closes by asking that all be done in Christ’s name, with thanks.
dc-46.setting: Joseph Smith dictated this revelation at Kirtland, Ohio, around 8 March 1831. The day in the earliest copy is hard to read but is probably the 8th. Members had begun keeping unbelievers out of their meetings, and some questioned the practice. Joseph had also met spiritual displays in the Ohio branches that he judged unsound. The revelation addressed both concerns for the whole Church.

verse.text: Wherefore, beware lest ye are deceived; and that ye may not be deceived seek ye earnestly the best gifts, always remembering for what they are given;

dc-47.summary: The revelation names John Whitmer to write and keep a regular history. He is also to help Joseph Smith copy all that is revealed. He may speak in meetings when it is fitting. He is to keep the church record and history continually. The reason given is that Oliver Cowdery has another office. If John is faithful, the Comforter will help him write.
dc-47.setting: This short revelation came at Kirtland, Ohio, around 8 March 1831. John Whitmer had already served as a scribe for Joseph Smith. He was asked to keep a history, but he said he would rather not. He agreed to serve if the Lord made his will known through Joseph. Joseph then dictated this revelation, and Whitmer accepted. One later copy dates it 7 March.

verse.text: Behold, it is expedient in me that my servant John should write and keep a regular history, and assist you, my servant Joseph, in transcribing all things which shall be given you, until he is called to further duties.

dc-48.summary: The revelation tells the Ohio members to stay where they live for now. Those who own land should share it with the eastern members. Those without land should buy for the present in nearby regions. All should save money and gain what they can in righteousness. That money will later buy land for an inheritance, “even the city”. The place of the city is not yet revealed. Men will be appointed to learn the place, buy the lands, and begin building. Then families will gather under the direction of the presidency and the bishop.
dc-48.setting: This revelation came at Kirtland, Ohio, on 10 March 1831. More than a hundred Church members from New York were expected to arrive soon. Earlier revelations had told them to gather to Ohio. Ohio members, including Bishop Edward Partridge, asked how to prepare for them. John Whitmer also wrote that some believed Ohio itself was the promised New Jerusalem.

verse.text: The place is not yet to be revealed; but after your brethren come from the east there are to be certain men appointed, and to them it shall be given to know the place, or to them it shall be revealed.

dc-49.summary: The revelation sends Sidney Rigdon and Parley P. Pratt to preach to the Shakers. Leman Copley is to go too, teaching only what the other two teach him. It says the Shakers want part of the truth, but not all, and must repent. It restates Peter’s message: believe, repent, be baptized, and receive the Holy Ghost. It says marriage is ordained of God and that meat is given for human use. It warns against wasting flesh and against one person possessing more than another. It says the Son of Man will not come as a woman or as a man traveling the earth. It ends with signs before Christ’s coming and a promise to go before them.
dc-49.setting: This revelation came at Kirtland, Ohio, on 7 May 1831. Leman Copley, a recent convert, had once belonged to the Shakers and kept some of their beliefs. Shakers taught that Christ had already returned in a woman, Ann Lee, and they practiced celibacy. Copley wanted his former community at North Union, near Cleveland, to hear the gospel. Joseph Smith asked the Lord about these questions. Sidney Rigdon read the revelation to the Shakers the next day, and they rejected it.

verse.text: And again, verily I say unto you, that the Son of Man cometh not in the form of a woman, neither of a man traveling on the earth.

dc-50.summary: The revelation warns the elders that false spirits are deceiving the world. It says there are hypocrites in the Church who will be detected. Then the Lord invites the elders to reason together, face to face. He asks what they were ordained to do, and answers: preach by the Spirit. Teaching and receiving by the Spirit of truth edifies both sides. What does not edify is darkness, and what is of God is light. For a spirit they cannot understand, they are to ask the Father in Jesus’s name. It sends Joseph Wakefield, Parley P. Pratt, and John Corrill to strengthen the churches, and calls Edward Partridge to repent.
dc-50.setting: This revelation came at Kirtland, Ohio, on 9 May 1831. Ohio branches had seen fainting, contortions, and claimed visions in their meetings. A local newspaper reported young converts rolling on floors. Joseph Smith had worked to curb these displays since February, but the problems went on. Elders who could not tell true spirits from false asked him for guidance.

verse.text: Wherefore, he that preacheth and he that receiveth, understand one another, and both are edified and rejoice together.

dc-51.summary: The revelation gives Edward Partridge directions for organizing the newly arrived people. He and his chosen helpers are to assign each family a portion by its needs. Each person receives a written deed that secures his portion. If a person transgresses and is judged unworthy to belong, he keeps only the deeded portion, not what he consecrated. An agent is to use the remaining money for food and clothing. The bishop is to keep a storehouse for whatever exceeds the people’s needs. The land is consecrated to them “for a little season”. Faithful, just, and wise stewards are promised eternal life.
dc-51.setting: This revelation came at Thompson, Ohio, on 20 May 1831. About sixty members from Colesville, New York, had just arrived under Newel Knight’s lead. They settled on land Leman Copley offered at Thompson. Bishop Edward Partridge was responsible for settling them under the law of consecration. He asked for direction, and Joseph Smith inquired of the Lord. Copley soon withdrew his offer, so the plan was not carried out there.

verse.text: Wherefore, let my servant Edward Partridge, and those whom he has chosen, in whom I am well pleased, appoint unto this people their portions, every man equal according to his family, according to his circumstances and his wants and needs.

routes.title: The Colesville Branch moves to Thompson, then Missouri

dc-52.summary: The revelation names Missouri as the site of the next conference. Joseph Smith and Sidney Rigdon are to travel there soon. If faithful, they will learn where the land of inheritance is. It pairs many other elders and sends them by different routes, preaching on the way. It warns Lyman Wight that Satan desires to sift him. It gives a pattern for knowing which spirits are of God. It sends Joseph Wakefield and Solomon Humphrey east and moves Heman Basset’s office to Simonds Ryder. It tells all elders to remember the poor, needy, sick, and afflicted.
dc-52.setting: This revelation came at Kirtland, Ohio, on 6 June 1831. It followed a Church conference held there in early June. At that conference, men were first ordained to the office of high priest. Participants also reported discerning and rebuking false spirits. Joseph Smith dictated the revelation that night and later said it came by vision.

verse.text: He that speaketh, whose spirit is contrite, whose language is meek and edifieth, the same is of God if he obey mine ordinances.

dc-53.summary: The revelation tells Sidney Gilbert that his prayers about his calling were heard. The voice speaks as the one crucified for the sins of the world. It commands him to forsake the world. He is to be ordained an elder to preach faith, repentance, and remission of sins. He is also to be an agent for the Church where the bishop appoints. He is to travel with Joseph Smith and Sidney Rigdon. More will be made known according to his labor, and only those who endure are saved.
dc-53.setting: This revelation came at Kirtland, Ohio, on 8 June 1831. Algernon Sidney Gilbert was a merchant and the business partner of Newel K. Whitney. Two days earlier, a revelation had named elders to go to Missouri, but not Gilbert. He then asked Joseph Smith to inquire about his own role. Gilbert left for Missouri with Joseph and Sidney Rigdon on 18 June.

verse.text: Behold, I, the Lord, who was crucified for the sins of the world, give unto you a commandment that you shall forsake the world.

dc-54.summary: The revelation speaks to Newel Knight and tells him to stand fast in his office. If his people want to escape their enemies, they must repent and become humble. It says the covenant they made has been broken and is now void. It pronounces woe on the one by whom the offense came. Those who kept the covenant will obtain mercy. The group is told to flee, choose a leader, and travel west to Missouri. There they are to earn a living until a place is prepared. It ends by urging patience in tribulation and promising rest.
dc-54.setting: This revelation came at Kirtland, Ohio, on 10 June 1831. The Colesville members had settled on Leman Copley’s farm in Thompson, Ohio. After the failed Shaker mission, Copley went back on the arrangement and ordered them off his land. The group was also divided over consecration, and some showed selfishness. Newel Knight, who presided over them, went to Kirtland to ask Joseph Smith what to do.

verse.text: And as the covenant which they made unto me has been broken, even so it has become void and of none effect.

routes.title: The Colesville Branch moves to Thompson, then Missouri

dc-55.summary: The revelation tells William Phelps that he is called and chosen. If baptized with an eye single to God’s glory, he will receive forgiveness and the Holy Spirit. Then Joseph Smith is to ordain him an elder to preach repentance and baptism. He may give the Holy Spirit to those who are contrite. He is to help Oliver Cowdery with printing and with writing books for schools. He is to travel with Joseph Smith and Sidney Rigdon to the land of inheritance. Joseph Coe is to go with them as well.
dc-55.setting: William W. Phelps was a newspaper editor and printer from Canandaigua, New York. He bought a Book of Mormon in 1830 and met Joseph Smith that December. In spring 1831 he spent thirty days in jail at Lyons, apparently over a debt. After his release, he moved his family to Ohio. He reached Kirtland by 14 June 1831, and Joseph Smith asked the Lord about him.

verse.text: And again, you shall be ordained to assist my servant Oliver Cowdery to do the work of printing, and of selecting and writing books for schools in this church, that little children also may receive instruction before me as is pleasing unto me.

dc-56.summary: The revelation opens with a warning to the rebellious among those who profess the Lord’s name. It says the Lord commands and also revokes as he sees fit. It cancels the mission of Marsh and Thayre and sends Selah J. Griffin with Marsh instead. It also cancels the mission of Griffin and Newel Knight because of rebellion at Thompson. Knight is to stay and lead the contrite there to Missouri. If Thayre repents of pride and selfishness, he may still go to Missouri; if not, he must take back his money and be cut off. If Joseph Smith must repay that money, the Lord promises to repay him in Missouri. The revelation ends with woes on selfish rich and greedy poor, and a blessing on the pure in heart.
dc-56.setting: Joseph Smith dictated this revelation in Kirtland, Ohio, on 15 June 1831. A revelation nine days earlier had paired Thomas B. Marsh and Ezra Thayre for a mission to Missouri. Marsh was ready to leave, but Thayre was not, so Marsh asked what to do. Thayre had paid money toward the farm where he lived and may have wanted a land title first. Meanwhile the Colesville Saints at Thompson wanted Newel Knight to stay and lead their move west.

verse.text: Wherefore I, the Lord, command and revoke, as it seemeth me good; and all this to be answered upon the heads of the rebellious, saith the Lord.

dc-57.summary: The revelation tells the elders gathered in Missouri that this land is appointed for the gathering of the Saints. It calls it the land of promise and the place for the city of Zion. Independence is the center place, and a temple lot lies west of the courthouse. The Saints are to buy land there and westward to the line “between Jew and Gentile,” as far as they can. Sidney Gilbert is to act as agent, buy land, and open a store. Edward Partridge is to divide inheritances to the Saints. William W. Phelps is to be printer, with Oliver Cowdery helping to copy and correct. These men are to settle in Zion, and the bishop and agent are to prepare for arriving families.
dc-57.setting: Joseph Smith reached Independence, Jackson County, Missouri, on 14 July 1831. A June revelation had sent him and other elders there from Ohio. Oliver Cowdery and other missionaries were already in the area after preaching to American Indians. Joseph Smith later wrote that he pondered those people and asked when and where Zion would be built. He dictated this revelation on 20 July; the original is lost.

verse.text: And thus saith the Lord your God, if you will receive wisdom here is wisdom. Behold, the place which is now called Independence is the center place; and a spot for the temple is lying westward, upon a lot which is not far from the courthouse.

dc-58.summary: The revelation tells the elders that blessings come after much tribulation. It says they were sent to obey, to lay Zion’s foundation, and to prepare a feast for the poor. Edward Partridge is to judge in Israel and divide inheritances, but he must repent of unbelief. The Saints must keep the laws of the land. The Lord will not command in all things, so people should do much good of their own free will. Martin Harris is to lay his money before the bishop, and he and Phelps must repent. Sidney Rigdon is to describe Zion in writing and dedicate the land and temple site. Joseph Smith, Rigdon, and Cowdery are to return home, Ziba Peterson loses his office, and others preach on the way.
dc-58.setting: Joseph Smith dictated this revelation in Jackson County on 1 August 1831, probably at Independence. Elders arriving in July found fewer than ten converts and a rough frontier town. Bishop Edward Partridge had disagreed with Joseph Smith over the quality of land being bought. That week Colesville Saints from Thompson, Ohio, also arrived. Many wanted to know the Lord’s will for them in the new gathering place.

verse.text: Verily I say, men should be anxiously engaged in a good cause, and do many things of their own free will, and bring to pass much righteousness;

dc-59.summary: The revelation blesses those who came to Zion with an eye single to God’s glory. Those who live will inherit the earth, and those who die will rest and receive a crown. It then gives commandments to love God and neighbor and not to steal, commit adultery, or kill. It asks for thanks in all things and the sacrifice of a broken heart and contrite spirit. The Saints are to go to the house of prayer and offer their sacraments on the Lord’s day. That day they are to rest, confess their sins, and prepare food with singleness of heart. If they do these things with thanks and glad hearts, the fulness of the earth is theirs. God is offended only by those who do not confess his hand in all things and do not obey.
dc-59.setting: Joseph Smith dictated this revelation in Jackson County, Missouri, on 7 August 1831. In the days before, the land had been dedicated for Zion and a temple site dedicated. That morning Polly Knight, wife of Joseph Knight Sr., died, the first Church member to die there. Sunday worship was lax among local settlers, and earlier Church laws said little about the Sabbath. Joseph Smith had been told to return to Ohio, so the Saints needed written guidance.

verse.text: And that thou mayest more fully keep thyself unspotted from the world, thou shalt go to the house of prayer and offer up thy sacraments upon my holy day;

dc-60.summary: The revelation tells the elders who are to return that the Lord is pleased they came. But some would not open their mouths and hid their talent for fear of man. If they are not more faithful, even what they have will be taken. The elders are to make or buy a boat and travel quickly toward Saint Louis. From there Sidney Rigdon, Joseph Smith, and Oliver Cowdery go to Cincinnati to preach. The rest go two by two and preach on the way home, not in haste. Edward Partridge is to give them money, to be repaid by those able. Elders still coming to Zion must not bury their talent and must shake off dust only in secret.
dc-60.setting: Joseph Smith dictated this revelation at Independence, Missouri, on 8 August 1831. The elders there had helped dedicate the land for Zion and the temple site. With that work done, many were anxious to go home. A later Joseph Smith history says they asked him what they should do. This revelation was his answer.

verse.text: But with some I am not well pleased, for they will not open their mouths, but they hide the talent which I have given unto them, because of the fear of man. Wo unto such, for mine anger is kindled against them.

routes.title: Return journey down the Missouri River

dc-61.summary: The revelation forgives the assembled elders who confess their sins with humble hearts. It says the whole company need not speed down the river while people on either side perish in unbelief. It says the Lord has decreed many destructions on these waters, but the faithful will not perish. Sidney Gilbert and William Phelps are to hurry ahead on their mission. It says the Lord blessed the waters in the beginning and cursed them in the last days through John. Joseph Smith, Sidney Rigdon, and Oliver Cowdery are to travel only by canal, and Saints bound for Zion are to go by land. The three are not to preach to the wicked until they reach Cincinnati. Reynolds Cahoon and Samuel Smith are to stay together, and the revelation closes with “be of good cheer” and a call to watch and pray.
dc-61.setting: Joseph Smith and about ten elders left Independence by canoe on the Missouri River in August 1831. On the third day they met dangers on the river and camped at McIlwaine’s Bend. Joseph Smith’s history says William W. Phelps saw the destroyer riding on the waters in vision. JSP editors note that this detail likely came from Phelps himself. Joseph Smith dictated this revelation on the riverbank on 12 August 1831.

verse.text: Nevertheless, all flesh is in mine hand, and he that is faithful among you shall not perish by the waters.

routes.title: Return journey down the Missouri River

dc-62.summary: The voice in verse 1 speaks as Jesus Christ, the elders’ advocate who knows human weakness. It tells the elders who have not reached Zion that their mission is not yet full. Their testimony is recorded in heaven, angels rejoice over them, and their sins are forgiven. They are to continue to Zion, hold a meeting, rejoice, and offer a sacrament. Afterward they may return together or two by two, as long as they are faithful. Those who wish may ride horses, mules, or carriages if they receive this with thanks. These matters are left to their judgment and the Spirit. The revelation ends: “I am with the faithful always.”
dc-62.setting: Joseph Smith and his companions were traveling home from Independence to Ohio in August 1831. On 13 August they crossed the Missouri River at Chariton, Missouri. There they met Hyrum Smith, John Murdock, David Whitmer, and Harvey Whitlock, still headed to Zion. Murdock had been ill, and he and Hyrum had stayed in Chariton while he recovered. After a joyful meeting, Joseph Smith dictated this revelation on the riverbank.

verse.text: Nevertheless, ye are blessed, for the testimony which ye have borne is recorded in heaven for the angels to look upon; and they rejoice over you, and your sins are forgiven you.

routes.title: Return journey down the Missouri River

dc-63.summary: The revelation opens with a warning to the wicked and rebellious. It says signs follow faith rather than create it, and it rebukes sign seekers and adulterers. The Saints are to gather to Zion, but not in haste. Zion can be gained only by purchase or by blood, and they are forbidden to shed blood. So Titus Billings is to sell the farm, and Newel K. Whitney and Oliver Cowdery are to raise money. The revelation describes the resurrection and the separation of the wicked at Christ’s coming. It rejects Sidney Rigdon’s written description of Zion and tells him to write another. It warns against using the Lord’s name without authority.
dc-63.setting: Joseph Smith, Sidney Rigdon, and Oliver Cowdery reached Kirtland from Missouri on 27 August 1831. They found that many members had left the Church while they were away. Joseph Smith later called the land of Zion the most important temporal concern of the time. He asked the Lord about gathering the Saints and buying land. He dictated this revelation on 30 August, probably at the Isaac Morley farm. Cowdery wrote the earliest surviving copy.

verse.text: But, behold, faith cometh not by signs, but signs follow those that believe.

routes.title: Return journey down the Missouri River

dc-64.summary: The revelation tells the elders that the Lord has forgiven their sins this once. Joseph Smith keeps the keys of the mysteries while he obeys, though he too has sinned. The elders must forgive all men, while the Lord forgives whom he will. Ezra Booth and Isaac Morley are named for not keeping the law, and Morley is forgiven. Edward Partridge has sinned and will be forgiven if he repents. Kirtland is to remain a strong hold for five years, so Frederick G. Williams keeps his farm.
